subject.title: [Bug] Race condition in approval-classifier.ts when tokenization exceeds max tokens

question: Does ACP-owner inspection of the upstream SDK confirm that permission callbacks cannot overlap or advance execution before `requestPermission` resolves, or should the reporter first supply a minimal protocol trace demonstrating that sequence?
rationale: Current OpenClaw source contradicts the described asynchronous-tokenization mechanism, but safely resolving an approval-bypass allegation requires owner confirmation of the upstream SDK sequencing contract.

options.title: Request protocol reproduction
options.body: Ask for the exact OpenClaw version, command payload, ACP request/response ordering, token-limit source, and a redacted trace or focused failing test before changing code.

options.title: Confirm SDK serialization
options.body: Have an ACP owner inspect the pinned SDK handler contract and close as non-reproducible if it guarantees the awaited sequencing observed in the client.

options.title: Sponsor defensive redesign
options.body: Treat all concurrent permission requests as unsupported and design an explicit serialized permission state machine after documenting the compatibility and deadlock implications.

recommendation.title: Request protocol reproduction
recommendation.body: Ask for the exact OpenClaw version, command payload, ACP request/response ordering, token-limit source, and a redacted trace or focused failing test before changing code.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work defines the current classifier allowlist and approval-hardening behavior at the center of the allegation.
